sources.entry: Part 8: Strings, forward references, and conclusion

summary.title: Let's write a compiler, part 8: Strings, forward references, and conclusion
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add Pascal-style string literals and forward procedure declarations to a PL/0 compiler written in C, finishing the compiler.
takeaways: Pascal string literals use single quotes, with '' for a literal quote; the lexer converts them to C string syntax, escaping double quotes.
Single-character strings are turned into C character literals to simplify code generation for writeChar-style output.
Forward declarations are added with a new forward token and stored in the symbol table, then accepted when the real procedure is defined.
symcheck is extended so that forward-declared names are treated as procedures, allowing mutually recursive procedures.
The compiler is considered complete at this point and the author moves on to a self-hosting compiler series.
summary.summary: The final part of a multi-part series building a PL/0 compiler in C. It adds string literal support: the lexer scans Pascal-style single-quoted strings, handles doubled quotes and C-style escapes, and emits the equivalent C string, while the parser and code generator are extended for writeStr. It then adds forward declarations, a new section in block() where a 'forward' keyword records procedure names in the symbol table, with addsymbol and symcheck adjusted so the later real definition is not flagged as a duplicate. The post closes by declaring the compiler finished and previewing a self-hosting compiler series.
